ai.description: The Abor Hills Agama reaches 20 cm in length. It is olive-brown with dark transverse bands and a distinct white stripe along the flanks. A prominent, serrated dorsal crest extends from the head to tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Abor Hills Agama is best distinguished by its distinct, elongated, and pointed snout that projects well beyond the lower jaw, unlike the blunter heads of other Japalura.
ai.habitat: The Abor Hills Agama inhabits dense, humid subtropical broadleaf forests in the Eastern Himalayas, typically found at elevations between 600 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Abor Hills agama is primarily diurnal, often observed basking on tree trunks or rocks to regulate its body temperature before actively foraging for small insects.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Japalura austeniana* is oviparous, laying clutches of 3–5 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between May and August in Northeast India.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Abor Hills Agama is endemic to the Eastern Himalayas, specifically occurring in the Abor Hills region of Arunachal Pradesh, India, at moderate elevations.
